t.etext: Since the 1991 Madrid Protocol, all mineral mining in Antarctica is banned except for research. Coal, iron ore and copper, and oil and gas in the surrounding seas, are thought to exist but cannot be developed. Most of the Earth's fresh water is locked in its ice. Economic activity today is almost entirely krill and toothfish fishing and Antarctic tourism, with catches set and managed under international agreements. Instead, many countries run bases to study climate, glaciers, space and life; Korea operates the King Sejong and Jang Bogo stations.
